title: Thermal-aware adaptive kernel gating for attention runtime (playbook + experiments)
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: We observe sporadic spikes in p95/p99 decode latency and occasional serving node throttling during sustained high-throughput workloads. Root cause analysis shows a correlation between elevated GPU temperature/power limits and degraded performance for FlashAttention v3 kernels in specific input-shape/sequence-length regions. Goals: 1) Design and implement a thermal-aware adaptive kernel gating layer that consults lightweight on-node telemetry (GPU temperature, SM clock, power headroom) before selecting a native attention kernel variant. 2) Create a playbook and automated rules for prefill/decode scheduling to avoid head-of-line thermal violations during bursts (e.g., delay or throttle non-critical prefill work; re-prioritize latency-sensitive requests). 3) Validate that the gating reduces tail latency during thermal stress with bounded throughput impact in steady-state, and integrates with existing fallback and rollout mechanisms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Implement kernel-gating decision path which can select between: FlashAttn v3, FlashAttn v2, quantized (int8) variant, and software fallback.
- Add lightweight on-node telemetry ingestion and expose a per-tenant thermal signal to routing layer.
- Define hysteresis and cooldown intervals to avoid oscillation.
- Automated canary rollout shows p99 tail latency improvement >= 10% under thermal stress tests, and steady-state throughput drop <= 5%.
- No new SLO violations in standard e2e regression suite.
- Playbook and runbook documented for on-call with thresholds and rollback steps.
experiment_plan: 1) Lab synthetic workload: sustained prefill-heavy generator at 90% node occupancy to reproduce thermal rise on A100 and H100 nodes. 2) Telemetry collection: GPU temp, SM clocks, power/thermal throttle flags, kernel-specific latencies, occupancy and batch size. 3) Implement gating prototype: decision rules based on temp thresholds + per-kernel confidence score derived from historical latency samples. 4) Run A/B: baseline routing vs gating routing across identical pools. 5) Collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, token/sec, and failure rates. 6) Tweak hysteresis and cooldown to minimize oscillation.
initial_results: Lab run (A100 40GB, 8-shard pool) under 12-minute sustained load: baseline p99 decode latency = 210ms; with thermal-aware gating enabled p99 = 172ms (-18%); throughput delta = -3.1%. Observed reduction in kernel fallback churn and 40% fewer kernel hotswaps during peak. Note: in sequences > 2k tokens the gating favored FlashAttn v2 at high temperature, which increased per-token cost by ~6% but lowered tail latency. These results are preliminary and require broader shape matrix testing.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Choosing safer kernels under thermal pressure reduces tail latency but can increase cost/throughput.
- Overly aggressive gating or short hysteresis can cause kernel oscillation (thrashing).
- Dependence on accurate/low-latency thermal telemetry; noisy signals can lead to mistaken gating.
- Extra routing decision adds negligible CPU overhead but introduces one more failure mode.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged canary on non-critical tenants (5% traffic) for 48h with aggressive telemetry. 2) If metrics pass, expand to 25% for 72h. 3) Monitor p99 tail, throughput, kernel hotswap count, and cost. 4) Gradual expansion to 100% with opt-out. 5) Add automated rollback rule if revocation threshold (p99 increase >5% or error rate >0.5%) hits.
next_steps:
- Finalize decision rule thresholds and hysteresis constants (T1/T2 and cooldown window).
- Add conversion of thermal flags into normalized 'thermal_score' consumed by the router.
- Implement telemetry dashboards and alerts for the new metrics.
- Schedule canary with Growth team on 2026-03-18.
- Pair with PM to craft customer communication for potential cost impact when gated kernels selected.
